rounds.text: The core investment risk for IMPAL lies in its profound inability to generate efficient returns on capital, as evidenced by a dismal ROCE of 4.6% and an ROE of 3.7% [E6, E7]. These figures suggest that the business is struggling to create value for shareholders, a reality further underscored by a trailing twelve-month sales growth rate that has decelerated to a meager 2% [E10]. While the bull case points to a multi-year sales uptrend [E63], this growth is significantly lagging behind the sector median of 19.3%, indicating a loss of competitive relevance [E71]. The market’s current expectations appear detached from operational reality, as evidenced by price growth outpacing profit growth by 4% [E48] and a scanX signal confirming that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E64]. Conceded: the stock trades at a low price-to-book ratio of 0.54x and offers a dividend yield of 3.01% [E2, E4]. Ultimately, the combination of stagnant long-term sales growth of 7.17% [E56] and poor capital efficiency makes the current P/E of 17.3x difficult to justify [E1].
